minutes.headline: Sewer Commission adopted a new grease trap log form and sent the One Main Street grease blockage to staff for inspection.
minutes.summary: The commission voted on an FY23 year-end commitment adjustment and adopted a new, more detailed grease trap log form. It discussed a grease blockage in the line near One Main Street and agreed staff will inspect the manhole and write to the restaurant owner. Permit fees, non-compliance fines and oil/water separator permitting were deferred to the July 25 agenda, and a revised encumbrance amount was voted.

budget_items.what_was_said: The regulations adopted in February set a fee lower than before; fees were waived during COVID. Deciding whether to implement it was deferred until more members are present.
The new regulations set an automatic fine and a daily amount for continued violation, replacing the earlier initial fee. Tabled for the next meeting.
The same annual fee and fine structure applies to oil water separators, which have never been permitted.
Staff plan more line jetting and manhole repairs this year, procured with three written quotes when under the procurement threshold.
Year-end figures could not be given because revenue was not current in the town accounting system.
The encumbrance was reduced after bills arrived before year end; the revised amount was voted.

Leominster IMA stays on each agenda; the engineers are tentatively invited for July 25.
An agenda will be prepared for a joint meeting with the Select Board next Tuesday at 7:30.
Someone else will host the August 8 meeting because the business manager will be absent.

A revised FY23 encumbrance amount passed; a separate vote on the FY23 year-end commitment adjustment was moved and seconded, but its outcome is not audible.

Restaurants and other businesses with grease traps or oil/water separators may face a permit fee and an automatic fine, and the rules are still undecided.
